title: A monotonic provenance contract must reject coverage regression, not merely describe monotonicity

observed: operations/continuity/schemas/provenance-state-transition.schema.json describes itself as a contract for monotonic provenance and coverage-state transitions.
The schema enumerates coverage_state values unknown, partial, complete_single_client, and exhaustive_reproduced.
The schema currently validates prior_state and new_state independently and contains no rule that rejects a lower new coverage_state after a higher prior coverage_state.
The schema's existing conditional rules constrain verified and unlocated_after_exhaustive_coverage outcomes but do not constrain general coverage regression.
inferred: A structurally valid record can currently claim exhaustive_reproduced coverage in prior_state and unknown coverage in new_state while still satisfying the schema.
Without an explicit transition relation, prose describing the contract as monotonic is stronger than the executable contract.
proposed: Define the admissible coverage transition relation explicitly before changing the schema.

At minimum, reject exhaustive_reproduced to complete_single_client, partial, or unknown; complete_single_client to partial or unknown; and partial to unknown unless a separately named evidence-revocation process is adopted.
Represent evidence revocation, if needed, as a distinct disputed or invalidated state rather than erasing previously attained coverage.
Add positive and adversarial validator fixtures before promoting any monotonicity amendment to authoritative use.
superseded: Treating the word monotonic in a schema description as sufficient machine-checkable enforcement.
Assuming independent validation of prior_state and new_state establishes a valid transition relation.
unresolved: The authoritative ordering and branching rules for origin_state have not been recovered in this run.
No validator fixture currently demonstrates acceptance or rejection of coverage regressions.
The schema has not been amended because the evidence-revocation semantics and complete origin-state transition graph require an authoritative decision source.

source_provenance.supports: The executable contract's description, coverage-state vocabulary, independent prior/new state validation, and existing conditional constraints.
The prior continuity record's claim that machine-checkable transition records should prevent structurally incomplete provenance changes, plus its explicit unresolved validator gap.
M-RECONCILE-002 remains the highest-priority continuity_mining item and requires provenance resolution without reconstructing unverified history.

verification.method: Inspected the exact current blobs for the transition schema, CM-1024, and ACTIVE_QUEUE; compared the schema description and enum vocabulary against its executable allOf constraints.
limitations: No JSON Schema validator was executed.
No authoritative origin-state ordering source was located.
This record identifies an enforcement gap; it does not assert that any historical transition actually regressed.

falsification_routes: Show an existing schema clause that rejects every descending coverage_state transition.
Validate an exhaustive_reproduced-to-unknown fixture against the current schema and demonstrate rejection by the schema itself.
Produce an authoritative decision source defining non-monotonic coverage semantics that supersedes the schema description.
